title: "Contributing"

order: 6
---

Anyone in the lab can edit this site. Small fixes can be made in the browser on GitHub. Bigger changes are easier on your own computer.

::: {.callout-important}
## This site is public
GitHub Pages sites can be read by anyone with the link. Never put passwords, app tokens, server addresses that should stay private, or unpublished data on any page.
:::

## Quick fix in the browser

Click **Edit this page** (under the table of contents on the right) on any page. GitHub opens the source file. Make the change and open a pull request. The site rebuilds after the pull request is merged into `main`.

## Working on your own computer

1. Install [Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/). RStudio and Positron already include it.
2. Clone this repository.
3. From the repository folder, run:

```bash
quarto preview
```

The site opens in your browser and reloads every time you save a file.

## Adding a page

1. Copy `_templates/page.qmd` into the folder for the section it belongs in, for example `protocols/fruit-firmness.qmd`. Use lowercase file names with hyphens.
2. Fill in `title`, `description`, and `order` at the top of the file.
3. Save. The page appears in the sidebar on its own. You do not need to edit `_quarto.yml`.

To add a whole new section, make a new folder containing an `index.qmd`. That page's `title` becomes the sidebar heading, and its `order` sets where the section appears.

## Images

Put images in an `images/` folder inside the section and always write alt text. See [Quarto syntax](quarto-syntax.qmd#images) for the format.

## Pages that run code

If a page runs R or Python code, render it on your computer before pushing (`quarto render path/to/page.qmd`) and commit the `_freeze/` folder along with your page. The GitHub build reuses those stored results and never runs your code, so it does not need R, Python, or your packages.

## Submitting changes

```bash
git switch -c fix-nextcloud-page     # new branch
# ...edit, preview, save...
git add .
git commit -m "Update Nextcloud folder structure"
git push -u origin fix-nextcloud-page
```

Then open a pull request on GitHub. Once it is merged into `main`, the site publishes in a few minutes.

## Writing guidelines

- One topic per page.
- Write steps that someone new can follow without asking you.
- Link to the source of truth (Breedbase, a pipeline's own repository) instead of copying details that change.
- If a step has a common failure, add a **Troubleshooting** section rather than burying it in the steps.
